data.name: IppRequestRejected
data.value: The print system at '{0}' rejected the request with IPP status '{1}'.
data.comment: {0} is the printer or server URI. {1} is the IPP status code name.

data.name: IppConnectionFailed
data.value: Could not communicate with the print system at '{0}'.
data.comment: {0} is the printer or server URI. The inner exception has the details.

data.name: IppConnectionTimedOut
data.value: The print system at '{0}' did not answer in time.
data.comment: {0} is the printer or server URI. Raised when the connection doesn't open within the connect timeout, or a request other than Print-Job doesn't finish within the response timeout.

data.name: IppUploadStalled
data.value: The printer at '{0}' stopped taking the document: nothing more could be sent to it for {1} seconds. Check the printer, then print the job again.
data.comment: {0} is the printer URI; {1} is IppNetworkOptions.UploadStallTimeout in seconds. Raised when a write of a Print-Job's document doesn't finish within the stall timeout.

data.name: IppResponseStalled
data.value: The printer at '{0}' was sent the whole document but did not answer within {1} seconds, so it is not known whether it will print it. Check the printer before printing the job again.
data.comment: {0} is the printer URI; {1} is IppNetworkOptions.UploadStallTimeout in seconds. Raised when no answer comes within the stall timeout of a Print-Job's document being sent. "Sent", not "received": the last of it may still be in the network's buffers.

data.name: IppTransferStalledSending
data.value: Nothing more of the request could be sent for {0} seconds.
data.comment: {0} is the stall timeout in seconds. The inner exception of IppUploadStalled.

data.name: IppTransferStalledAwaitingResponse
data.value: No answer came within {0} seconds of the request being sent.
data.comment: {0} is the stall timeout in seconds. The inner exception of IppResponseStalled.

data.name: IppAuthenticationRequired
data.value: The print system at '{0}' needs a user name and password for this request.
data.comment: {0} is the printer or server URI. Raised for HTTP 401 or IPP client-error-not-authenticated when no credentials were configured.

data.name: IppCredentialsRejected
data.value: The print system at '{0}' did not accept the user name and password.
data.comment: {0} is the printer or server URI. Raised for HTTP 401 or IPP client-error-not-authenticated when credentials were sent.

data.name: IppEncryptedAuthenticationRequired
data.value: The print system at '{0}' needs a user name and password, sent over an encrypted connection, for this request.
data.comment: {0} is the printer or server URI. Raised for HTTP 426 when no credentials were configured: CUPS asks for encryption before it asks for a password.

data.name: IppEncryptionRequired
data.value: The print system at '{0}' only accepts the user name and password over an encrypted connection, but encryption is turned off.
data.comment: {0} is the printer or server URI. Raised for HTTP 426 when credentials were configured without encryption.

data.name: IppRequestForbidden
data.value: The print system at '{0}' does not allow this user to make this request.
data.comment: {0} is the printer or server URI. Raised for HTTP 403 or IPP client-error-not-authorized.

data.name: IppSecureConnectionFailed
data.value: Could not open an encrypted connection to the print system at '{0}'. CUPS servers use a self-signed certificate unless given another, which isn't trusted by default: check it in a server certificate validation callback.
data.comment: {0} is the printer or server URI. The inner exception has the TLS failure, such as an untrusted certificate.

data.name: IppResponseUnreadable
data.value: The print system at '{0}' sent an answer Latiprimere can't read.
data.comment: {0} is the printer or server URI. The inner exception says what couldn't be read, such as an answer cut short, a number too large or a value of the wrong type.

data.name: IppResponseNotIpp
data.value: The address '{0}' answered, but not with IPP. It may be a web page, such as a printer's or CUPS's web interface, rather than the IPP address of a printer or print server.
data.comment: {0} is the printer or server URI. Raised when the answer's Content-Type isn't application/ipp.

data.name: PrinterNoLongerAvailable
data.value: The printer at '{0}' could no longer be found.
data.comment: {0} is the printer URI.

data.name: IppResponseMissingJob
data.value: The print system at '{0}' accepted the job but did not return its job ID.
data.comment: {0} is the printer URI.

data.name: OutputFileNotSupported
data.value: IPP and CUPS printers cannot print to a file. Remove PrintOptions.OutputFile, or use a Windows printer.

data.name: DocumentFormatUnknown
data.value: Printing over IPP doesn't support documents of format '{0}'.
data.comment: {0} is a DocumentFormat value this version of Latiprimere.Ipp doesn't know, such as one added in a later version of Latiprimere.Abstractions.

data.name: DocumentFormatNotSupportedByPrinter
data.value: The printer does not accept '{0}' documents. It accepts: {1}.
data.comment: {0} is the MIME type sent, {1} the comma-separated MIME types the printer reports.

data.name: VendorOptionValueEmpty
data.value: The vendor option '{0}' has an empty value. Separate several values with single commas.
data.comment: {0} is the key, such as ipp:finishings.

data.name: VendorOptionNameInvalid
data.value: The vendor option '{0}' doesn't name an IPP attribute: after the prefix, use lower-case letters, digits, '-', '_' and '.', starting with a letter, such as ipp:print-quality.
data.comment: {0} is the key as given.

data.name: VendorOptionSetByLatiprimere
data.value: The vendor option '{0}' sets {1}, which Latiprimere already sends for this job, from PrintOptions or for the request itself. Use the typed option instead, or leave it at its default.
data.comment: {0} is the key, {1} the IPP attribute name, such as copies.

data.name: VendorOptionSetTwice
data.value: The vendor options '{0}' and '{1}' both set {2}. Use one of them.
data.comment: {0} and {1} are the keys, such as ipp:print-quality and cups:print-quality; {2} the IPP attribute name.

data.name: PclmNotOneBit
data.value: PCLm has no 1-bit form: its pages are 8-bit grey or 24-bit colour.

data.name: AppleRasterNotOneBit
data.value: Apple raster has no 1-bit form: its pages are 8-bit grey or 24-bit colour.

data.name: IppCertificateNotTrusted
data.value: The printer at '{0}' presented a certificate that isn't trusted, with SHA-256 fingerprint {1}. If that is the fingerprint the printer's own web page shows, add it to IppNetworkOptions.TrustedCertificateFingerprints to trust it.
data.comment: {0} is the printer URI, {1} the certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint as colon-separated hexadecimal pairs.

data.name: IppCertificateNotVouchedForCredentials
data.value: The printer at '{0}' presented a certificate the system trusts, with SHA-256 fingerprint {1}, but the password in IppNetworkOptions.Credentials goes only to printers configured in PrinterUris or PrinterCredentials, or whose certificate is pinned or accepted by ServerCertificateValidationCallback. If that is the fingerprint the printer's own web page shows, add it to IppNetworkOptions.TrustedCertificateFingerprints, or configure the printer by its URI.
data.comment: {0} is the printer URI, {1} the certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint as colon-separated hexadecimal pairs.

data.name: IppRequestWithoutPrinterUri
data.value: The IPP request has no printer-uri to send it to.

data.name: IppCertificateFingerprintInvalid
data.value: '{0}' isn't a SHA-256 fingerprint: it needs 32 bytes in hexadecimal, such as 3A:7F:… with 32 pairs.
data.comment: {0} is the value given in IppNetworkOptions.TrustedCertificateFingerprints.

data.name: IppCredentialsWithoutUserName
data.value: Credentials in IppNetworkOptions have no user name. Set its UserName, or leave them unset to send none.

data.name: IppCredentialsUserNameHasColon
data.value: A user name in IppNetworkOptions' credentials can't contain ':', which HTTP Basic authentication uses to separate it from the password.

data.name: IppPrinterCredentialsUriInvalid
data.value: '{0}' in IppNetworkOptions.PrinterCredentials isn't an absolute ipp or ipps URI.
data.comment: {0} is the URI given.

data.name: IppCredentialsNeedIpps
data.value: The printer at '{0}' asks for a user name and password, which Latiprimere sends only over an encrypted connection. Print to its ipps:// address instead.
data.comment: {0} is the printer URI, an ipp:// one.

data.name: IppAuthenticationSecureAddress
data.value: It lists '{0}' as its encrypted address: print to that, with a user name and password set for it.
data.comment: Added to a PrintAuthenticationException's message. {0} is an ipps:// URI from the printer's printer-uri-supported, at the host it was reached at.

data.name: IppAuthenticationMethodNotSupported
data.value: It asks for '{0}' authentication, which Latiprimere can't give: it sends a user name and password with HTTP Basic only.
data.comment: Added to a PrintAuthenticationException's message. {0} is the printer's uri-authentication-supported keyword, such as digest, certificate or negotiate.

data.name: ImageNotJpeg
data.value: The document isn't a JPEG image: it doesn't start as one.

data.name: ImageJpegDamaged
data.value: The JPEG image is damaged: it ends before its frame header, or a segment runs past its end.

data.name: ImageJpegCodingUnsupported
data.value: The JPEG image uses a coding PDF can't carry, such as lossless, hierarchical or arithmetic coding. Save it as a baseline or progressive JPEG to print it.

data.name: ImageJpegPrecisionUnsupported
data.value: The JPEG image has {0} bits a sample; only 8 can be printed.
data.comment: {0} is the bits in each sample.

data.name: ImageJpegComponentsUnsupported
data.value: The JPEG image has {0} colour components; grey (1), colour (3) and CMYK (4) can be printed.
data.comment: {0} is the number of components.

data.name: ImageNotPng
data.value: The document isn't a PNG image: it doesn't start with PNG's signature.

data.name: ImagePngChunkDamaged
data.value: The PNG image is damaged at its {0} chunk.
data.comment: {0} is the four-letter chunk type, such as IHDR.

data.name: ImagePngDataDamaged
data.value: The PNG image is damaged: its image data ends early, or can't be decompressed.

data.name: ImagePngHeaderInvalid
data.value: The PNG image's header isn't valid: {0} by {1} pixels, bit depth {2}, colour type {3}.
data.comment: {0} and {1} are the width and height, {2} the bit depth and {3} the colour type.

data.name: ImageTooLarge
data.value: The image is {0} by {1} pixels; images up to 100000 pixels across and down, and 300 million pixels in all, can be printed.
data.comment: {0} and {1} are the width and height in pixels.

data.name: ImageFileTooLarge
data.value: The image is {0} bytes; image files up to 2 GB can be printed.
data.comment: {0} is the file's size in bytes.

data.name: ConvertedDocumentNotSupportedByPrinter
data.value: The printer doesn't accept {0} documents, and Latiprimere can't convert them for it: it accepts {1}. Images and text are converted to PDF, and for a printer that doesn't take PDF rendered as raster, which needs a PDF rasteriser, such as Latiprimere.Rendering.Pdfium, and a raster format the printer takes in IppNetworkOptions.RasterFormats.
data.comment: {0} is the image or text MIME type, {1} the comma-separated MIME types the printer reports.

data.name: TextCharacterUnsupported
data.value: The text can't be printed: line {1}, column {2} has the character {0}, which Courier can't show without an embedded font. Text Latiprimere lays out is limited to the Windows-1252 characters, which cover Western European languages, and to tabs, line breaks and form feeds among control characters. CUPS lays text out itself, without this limit; otherwise print the text as a PDF.
data.comment: {0} is the code point, such as U+4E2D; {1} and {2} the line and column, from 1.

data.name: PdfRasterFormatsExcluded
data.value: The printer doesn't accept PDF documents, and the raster formats it takes, {0}, are left out of the ones PDFs may be rendered into: add them to IppNetworkOptions.RasterFormats, or WindowsOptions.IppRasterFormats, to print PDFs to it.
data.comment: {0} is the comma-separated MIME types of the raster formats the printer takes.

data.name: PdfNeedsRasterizerForPrinter
data.value: The printer doesn't accept PDF documents; it accepts: {0}. PDFs can be printed to it as raster images with a PDF rasteriser: add Latiprimere.Rendering.Pdfium and call AddLatiprimerePdfium(), or pass a PdfiumRasterizer to IppNetworkPrintSystemFactory.Create.
data.comment: {0} is the comma-separated MIME types the printer reports.

data.name: RasterNoResolution
data.value: The printer accepts '{0}' but lists no resolution for it with the same dots per inch across and down, up to 2400 dpi, which Latiprimere needs.
data.comment: {0} is the raster MIME type.

data.name: RasterPageTooLarge
data.value: A page of {0} × {1} mm at {2} dpi would be more than {3} pixels across or down, more than Latiprimere renders. Choose a smaller paper size, or a lower IppNetworkOptions.MaxRenderDpi.
data.comment: {0} and {1} are the paper's width and height in millimetres, {2} the resolution, {3} the most pixels allowed.

data.name: RasterNoColorSpace
data.value: The printer accepts '{0}' but lists no colour space for it that Latiprimere can send: 8-bit grey, 24-bit sRGB or 1-bit black.
data.comment: {0} is the raster MIME type.

data.name: RasterMediaUnknown
data.value: A PDF sent as raster needs the paper size, and the printer's default paper '{0}' doesn't give it. Choose one with PrintOptions.MediaSize.
data.comment: {0} is the printer's media-default keyword, or empty if it reports none.

data.name: PdfHeaderCommentInvalid
data.value: The PDF header comment '{0}' must be one line of printable ASCII.
data.comment: {0} is the comment given. An internal error: Latiprimere writes its own comments.

data.name: PdfObjectNotReserved
data.value: PDF object {0} isn't reserved, or is written already.
data.comment: {0} is the object number. An internal error in the PDF writer.

data.name: PdfObjectNotWritten
data.value: PDF object {0} was reserved but never written.
data.comment: {0} is the object number. An internal error in the PDF writer.

data.name: PdfFileFinished
data.value: The PDF file is finished, so nothing more can be written to it.
data.comment: An internal error in the PDF writer.

data.name: PdfPageAlreadyStarted
data.value: A PDF page is started already: end it before starting another.
data.comment: An internal error in the PDF writer.

data.name: PdfPageNotStarted
data.value: No PDF page is started: start one first.
data.comment: An internal error in the PDF writer.

data.name: PdfPageNotEnded
data.value: The PDF page wasn't ended before the document was.
data.comment: An internal error in the PDF writer.

data.name: PdfDocumentWithoutPages
data.value: A PDF document needs at least one page.
data.comment: An internal error in the PDF writer.

data.name: PdfImageInvalid
data.value: A PDF image needs a width and height of at least 1, 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 bits per sample, and either a filter for data compressed already or an encoding for the writer, not both.
data.comment: An internal error in the PDF writer.

data.name: PdfTextCharacterUnsupported
data.value: The character {0}, at position {1}, can't be printed: text is set in Courier, which shows the Windows-1252 characters of Western European languages.
data.comment: {0} is the character's code, such as U+0100; {1} its zero-based position in the text.

data.name: PdfPasswordNotSupported
data.value: The PDF is password-protected, and the printer at {0} can neither be sent its password nor be sent its pages as raster.
data.comment: {0} is the printer URI. Never include the password.

data.name: PageRangesSelectNoPages
data.value: The page ranges {0} leave no pages of a document of {1} pages.
data.comment: {0} lists the ranges; {1} is the page count.

data.name: PageRangesNotForRawData
data.value: Page ranges can't be applied to raw printer data, whose pages Latiprimere can't see. Leave PrintOptions.PageRanges empty for raw jobs.
data.comment: Thrown when a raw job sets PrintOptions.PageRanges.

data.name: FinishingNotSupported
data.value: The finishing {0} isn't one this version of Latiprimere's IPP support knows.
data.comment: {0} is the Finishing value.
